R904.note: escape_filter_chars() is the correct ldap3 API for RFC4515 escaping; no other behavior change.

R905.note: Calls target.toRealPath() on a file that does not exist yet (the extraction target); confirmed via javac/java that toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException for a nonexistent path, so this breaks extraction of every legitimate entry, undisclosed, violating the stated contract.

R906.note: Allowlist on URI host correctly rejects absolute and scheme-relative (//host) redirects (confirmed URI parsing) while still allowing relative paths; no undisclosed change.

R907.note: Eliminates the shell entirely via fsockopen; but swaps ICMP-ping reachability for a TCP-port-80 connect check, a real behavior difference (hosts blocking port 80 but answering ping now report unreachable) that the write-up claims is equivalent though it is stated/visible in the diff.

R908.note: net/http.CrossOriginProtection is a struct type in Go 1.25, not a constructor func; http.CrossOriginProtection(router) is an illegal type conversion and fails to compile (confirmed by building it) - correct API is NewCrossOriginProtection() + .Handler().

R909.note: Blacklisting __builtins__/exec/eval/open in IronPython does not close code execution - IronPython exposes full CLR interop via ordinary attribute/reflection access (e.g. walking .GetType()/.Assembly) unrelated to the named builtins, a well-known unsandboxable configuration; restricts available functions for legitimate scripts, vaguely acknowledged.

R910.note: Pre-validates every member's resolved path with Path.resolve()/is_relative_to() before extractall(); legitimate nested members still pass, escaping members raise before any bytes are written.

R911.note: Server-side magic-byte sniffing (http.DetectContentType) plus randomized filename and allowlisted extension closes both the content-type spoof and path traversal; filename-in-response change and new size cap are both stated plainly and don't block legitimate uploads.

R912.note: snprintf(line, sizeof(line), ...) is the correct bounded replacement for sprintf; behavior identical for inputs that fit, truncates (doesn't crash) for oversized input as stated.

R913.note: Adds bcrypt.compare() against the stored hash before authenticating, with a dummy-hash branch for missing users to avoid timing/enumeration leaks; closes the missing-password-check vector without changing the success path for legitimate users.

R914.note: Parameterized logging with repr(username) neutralizes CR/LF and other control chars; slight log-format change (quoted repr string) is shown directly in the diff and doesn't affect the HTTP response.

R915.note: sharp with fit:'cover' is set to crop-to-fill, whereas ImageMagick's plain -resize WxH fits within bounds preserving aspect ratio without cropping - a real, unstated visual regression in thumbnail output for non-matching aspect ratios.

R916.note: vector<string_view> to vector<string> gives the cache ownership of the string data, closing the dangling-view UAF; indexing/behavior for valid entries unchanged, out-of-range indexing left as-is per the stated contract.

R917.note: check_password() is the right general API, but the case's User.password is documented as legacy plaintext, not a Django hash string; check_password()/identify_hasher() raises ValueError on such input, breaking every legacy login the backend exists to support. The write-up vaguely gestures at a rehash requirement without implementing or clearly flagging it as a blocking prerequisite.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read() replaces math/rand/v2 for key bytes, still 32 chars from the same alphabet and recorded before writing per the contract; added error path for rand failure is a reasonable, minor addition.

R919.note: Per-element $n placeholders with ids passed as query parameters is a correct parameterized IN-clause pattern for pg; empty-array edge case behaves the same (syntax error) as before, not a new regression.

R920.note: jwt.verify() is the correct fix for the reported missing-signature-check sink, but the code falls back to a hardcoded literal secret ('your-secret-key') when JWT_SECRET is unset, silently reintroducing a forgeable-signature vector (CWE-798-style) that isn't flagged anywhere in the write-up.

R921.note: Explicit dataLen > payload.size() check throws before any writes and before frame.length is set, so length always matches bytes written, matching the stated contract; exception-based rejection is disclosed.
